angle_gap: The page blends employer process guidance with candidate-facing prep advice in the same article ('How candidates should answer', 'How candidates can prepare' sit inside a guide addressed to employers), and its example answers are generic templates ('I oversaw the development of my sales team which led to a 20% increase') with no behaviorally-anchored scoring rubric per competency — it names 'How should employers score competency based interviews?' as a section but gives no structured scale, just prose.
asset: How to Score Competency-Based Interviews So Every Recruiter Rates the Same Answer the Same Way
distinct_angle: Strips out the candidate-prep sections Thomas mixes in and replaces their generic example answers with a behaviorally-anchored rating scale per competency, giving recruiters a scorecard they can actually run consistently — the structure and scoring depth this page lacks.
